Article Title: Only talks can resolve issues, hope Bangladesh PM visits India soon: Trivedi
Article Text:
Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi

DHAKA: Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi has said differences between the two neighbours can only be resolved through talks and expressed hope PM Tarique Rahman’s visit to India “should take place much sooner”.His remarks on Sunday came hours after Bangladesh govt attached tough conditions for New Delhi prior to Tarique’s possible bilateral visit to India at PM Narendra Modi’s invitation — “act expeditiously on extradition of Sheikh Hasina and other criminal fugitives, and help create a ‘propitious environment’ for him to make the visit”.Calling challenges an inherent part of democracy, Trivedi said Bangladesh and India are two sovereign countries and don’t merely share a border but also “share a dream”. “We have our challenges. There is no doubt about it. If you do not have challenges, that is not democracy,” he said while at a welcome dinner in Dhaka. “Issues can only be sorted out by meeting,” he said, expressing optimism that PM Tarique’s India visit will take place “much sooner”.Describing both PMs as “people’s persons”, he asserted when the two leaders meet and interact, no issue could be left unaddressed. Trivedi also acknowledged that the two sovereign countries would have differences and need space to pursue their respective interests.Meanwhile, an Indian business delegation from CII began its three-day Bangladesh visit Monday, seeking to further strengthen the economic and commercial engagement between nations. The India delegation, led by CII director general Chandrajit Banerjee, comprises 14 business leaders.
Article Summary: Indian high commissioner to bangladesh dinesh trivedi said differences between the two neighbours can only be resolved through talks. He expressed hope pm tarique rahman’s visit to india “should take place much sooner’ bangladeshi govt attached tough conditions for new delhi prior to tarique's possible bilateral visit.

Article Title: Lakshmi Mittal's Ukraine steel plant hit by Russian missile; 2 killed
Article Text:

Russian attacks on Ukraine on Sunday struck a site at ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, the country’s largest steel producer owned by Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal , killing two people and injuring over 10 workers and contractors, the company told Kyiv Post.The missile strike hit the ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih mining and metallurgical plant in the central city of Kryvyi Rih on August 16, forcing the company to partially suspend operations.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others. He also reported one death in the northeastern city of Sumy.ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, the Ukrainian unit of the world’s second-largest steelmaker, confirmed that one of its sites was hit in the missile attack.The strikes also caused casualties and damage elsewhere in Ukraine. In the southern Zaporizhzhia region, a man and a woman were killed after their home was hit, according to Ivan Fedorov, head of the regional military administration.In Kyiv, Russian attacks sparked several fires and injured six people. A major fire broke out at one of the capital’s largest book markets near the Pochaina metro station, destroying rows of closely packed kiosks and sending thick plumes of black smoke into the sky.“Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure,” Zelenskyy said.Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih as well as several military-industrial facilities in Kyiv, including a site involved in manufacturing Ukraine’s Flamingo missiles.The Ukrainian-made long-range missiles have become increasingly important to Kyiv’s attacks on Russian territory. Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Ukraine had used the weapons to strike a rocket research and production centre in Samara, about 900 km (560 miles) from the Ukrainian border.The escalating conflict between the two neighbouring countries saw Ukraine launch one of its largest aerial attacks on Russia, killing at least six people on Sunday.Ukraine unleashed hundreds of drones across Russia, with Kyiv stepping up long-range strikes on military and energy facilities as well as major commercial sites.Russia’s defence ministry said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight, including hundreds headed towards Moscow. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said around 600 drones were detected near the capital.An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone struck a home in the Moscow region, while another attack sparked a fire at a Wildberries warehouse in Podolsk.Ukraine also came under heavy Russian attack, with drone strikes destroying homes and setting fire to Kyiv’s landmark book market.

Article Title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I won't speak': Ex-officer recalls PM Modi's demand on I-Day 2014
Article Text:
PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," the officer recalled.

Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014.Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15. The officials had specifically discussed the bulletproof glass barrier placed in front of the Prime Minister."Me and the Director of Intelligence Bureau (IB), went to PM Modi for a briefing before August 15 because it was his first Independence Day where he would address the country from the ramparts of the Red Fort (as the Prime Minister).""During that conversation we explained him (PM Modi) that there is a barrier in front of him which is the bulletproof glass. PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," he told news agency IANS.Mathur said security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. The location offers a wide view of the surrounding area, including buildings in Chandni Chowk, making security arrangements particularly sensitive."From our side, this was naturally a security issue. As people know, the entire Chandni Chowk area is visible from there (Red Fort) where there are many buildings. That is why, from a security standpoint we urged the Prime Minister to rethink his decision. However, PM Modi clearly stated that if this (bulletproof shield) is not removed, he will not address."The former defence secretary said the security team eventually agreed to Modi's demand and removed the glass barrier just hours before the Independence Day ceremony."Due to this, I and the director of IB changed our standpoint and decided to remove the bulletproof glass. This glass shield was then removed on the intervening night of August 14 and 15, at about 2 am," Mathur added.The episode was recalled as Modi once again departed from established security protocol during the 80th Independence Day celebrations on Saturday, when he met schoolchildren, NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers at the Red Fort after his address.During the interaction, a young girl approached Modi and bent down to touch his feet. As she did so, her cap slipped from her head and fell to the ground.Modi immediately bent down, picked up the cap and placed it back on the girl's head. The gesture drew smiles and applause from the children and people around them.

Security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. Article Title: Supreme Court declares August 22 full working day in place of holiday on August 27
Article Text:
The Supreme Court in New Delhi. The Court and its Registry will remain closed on August 27, 2026, with August 22 designated a full working day under the revised schedule. (Photo: ANI)

The Supreme Court circular dated August 14, 2026, declares Thursday, August 27, a holiday for the Court and its Registry. Saturday, August 22, will be a full working day, with Registry offices functioning until 5pm. (Photo: ANI)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court and its Registry will remain closed on Thursday, August 27, 2026, while Saturday, August 22, will be a full working day after the Full Court accepted a request for the additional holiday.The change followed a request from the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA), according to a circular issued by the Supreme Court's Administrative General Branch.The revised schedule will leave the Court and Registry closed for three consecutive days, from August 26 to August 28. The Court calendar already lists August 26 and August 28 as holidays.The Supreme Court and its Registry will work a full day on August 22 to make up for the August 27 holiday. Registry offices will remain open until 5pm that Saturday.
Article Summary: The supreme court and its registry will remain closed on august 27, 2026. Saturday, august 22, will be a full working day, with registry offices functioning until 5pm. The change followed a request from the supreme court advocates-on-record association.

Article Title: How PM Modi has changed focus of Independence Day speeches
Article Text:
As the country has progressed, so has the theme of PM Modi’s speeches.

In all 13 speeches, PM Modi focused on taking the country forward.

NEW DELHI: From access to aspiration and from problems to potential - the focus of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speeches has kept changing since 2014.Those tracking his speeches over the last 12 years have noted how in the initial year, Prime Minister Modi focused on issues such as toilets, bank accounts, poverty and fertiliser shortages. That has given way to attention to priorities like 6G, semiconductor, AI and quantum computing.If 2014 had mention of toilets as a challenge, Saturday he renewed his pitch for women's reservation in legislature. "In the early years of Modi govt, the speeches were often about problems that we may today consider ordinary. But PM's tone was urgent when he addressed them. The challenge was to fix what was broken, reach those who had been left out," said an official.As the country has progressed, so has the theme of his speeches, with a constant nudge to move to the next level, while setting the bar high, officials said.In all his 13 speeches so far, the pitch has always been on taking the country forward and ensuring everyone in society benefits from the gains and the schemes."Over the years, his vocabulary began to change. The conversation moved from plugging gaps to building capabilities, from solving immediate problems to creating systems that could prevent those problems from defining India again," the official added.In 2014, Prime Minister Modi called for eradicating poverty. Over the years, the focus has shifted to building a developed nation as poverty levels fell and crores moved out of extreme poverty.So, in Prime Minister Modi's 2026 speech, he underlined how social security cover has seen a four-fold jump to 100 crore citizens in the last 12 years.Women have remained a prominent theme over the past 12 years.If in 2014 he highlighted the plight of women who had to wait for sunset to venture out to ease themselves in the open since they did not have access to toilets, by 2018, the attention had moved to permanent commission for women in the armed forces.And, in his latest speech, PM Modi underlined the need for 33% reservation for women in legislatures, for which he sought the opposition's support.The shift is also visible in the focus on farmers - from preventing farmer suicides to tapping global markets through FTAs.
Article Summary: As the country has progressed, so has the theme of pm modi’s speeches. In all 13 speeches, pm modi focused on taking the country forward. The shift is also visible in the focus on farmers - from preventing farmer suicides to tapping global markets through ftas.

NEW DELHI: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Monday defended Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's "dimagi naxal" remarks by invoking former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh 's 20-year-old assessment of the threat.In a social media post on X, Rijiju shared former PM's speech in which he had said that "naxalism is the single biggest internal security challenge ever faced by our country.""Congress party must apologise & say sorry to the Family of former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji," Rijiju said.This comes after PM Modi, during his Independence Day speech, said that while Naxals who took up arms in the jungle have been eliminated, there are also "dimagi naxals", who are in various parts of the country and need to be "identified and isolated.""For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives. My dear countrymen, we have been able to curb and free the country from 'hathariya naxal' (armed naxal)," The Prime Minister said."Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path.We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," he added.The opposition latched on to PM Modi's remarks and dismissed it as a hollow political rhetoric.Senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that the term carries no real substance, drawing a parallel to previous debates surrounding the phrase "urban naxal"."Two or three years ago, he (PM Modi) called his political opponents 'urban naxals'; at that time, the question arose in Parliament as to what the definition of 'Urban Naxal' was. The home minister replied that there is no such thing as an 'urban naxal,' nor is there any definition for it. Today, the Prime Minister is using the term 'mental naxal' (ideological Naxal) for his political opponents from the Red Fort," Jairam Ramesh alleged.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal also targeted PM Modi and said that he is a "dimagi naxal" because he is a patriot."Yes. I am a dimagi naxal. Because I am a patriot. And I am proud of it," kejriwal said in a post on X.Earlier, on Sunday Rijiju had said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on "dimagi naxals" were not meant for the opposition leader and said that "dimagi naxals" referred only to those who supported Maoists and rejected Constitution."PM Narendra Modi ji didn't say opposition leaders as dimagi naxals," Rijiju said in a social media post on X."Only following are dimagi naxals: 1. Who support Maoists and reject Indian Constitution. 2. Who stand with separatists & support Article 370. 3. Who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he added.

Article Title: Indian handle quoted by Netanyahu & US: How a false claim fooled the world
Article Text:
Hawkish narrative got significant boost from a fake quote.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tehran's alleged effort to develop nuclear weapons has been the key reason cited by US President Trump and Israel govt for the war on Iran. In recent weeks, amid stop-start peace efforts, the hawkish narrative got a significant boost from a fake quote first posted by an Indian X handle, which then raced through Tel Aviv-Washington political and diplomatic circles, right up to PM Benjamin Netanyahu and White House."Alert," the account, @RealBababanaras, posted on Aug 5, "While world is expecting peace, IRGC Chief Ahmad Wahidi again threatened -'There will be no talk on Enriched Urenium (sic) or nuclear weapons, as long as US & Israel are owning nuclear weapons, we will keep working on it for national security. If they dispose, we will dispose." This reference was to Brig Gen Ahmad Vahidi, head of Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and one of Iran's powerful military figures.In less than two hours, another India-based account, @Im_Ritikaa, posted a paraphrased version in Hindi.Neither cited any sources. An Israeli news outlet, YNet, and The New York Times have since reported that there is no evidence this statement was ever made by Vahidi. But the posts on Indian X had already found resonance in Israeli media. By the afternoon of Aug 5, Mossad Commentary, a prominent Israeli account (but not affiliated with Israel's intelligence agency, Mossad), published the fake statement with a comment: "The regime is not preparing to abandon its nuclear ambitions.It is buying time. There will be no deal." The post was seen more than 300,000 times by Aug 17.About half an hour later, Israeli broadcaster Channel 14 English posted it as news, with its own comment: "This is the first time an Iranian official has admitted to developing a nuclear bomb." The post had almost 450,000 views at the time of filing this report.By evening, Israel PM Netanyahu's son Yair had reposted both. From there, the claim made a short leap to Netanyahu's podium. At a state ceremony in Jerusalem honouring the family of Theodor Herzl, the founder of modern political Zionism, Netanyahu presented it as fact. "Today we heard Revolutionary Guards commander Vahidi explicitly declaring Iran's intention to continue to develop nuclear weapons," he said. "Continue! That is what he said. Well, as prime minister of Israel, I too am determined to continue preventing Iran from possessing nuclear weapons."Within minutes, US ambassador to UN, Mike Waltz, reposted the claim - as did American Conservative commentator Mark Levin and Republican senator Rick Scott later. By the night of Aug 5, it had made its way to Fox News (which clarified later the claim had been "taken out of context and amplified").The actual Vahidi comment, it said, was based on one made in 2025 - that Iran's position on nuclear weapons had been transparent, and Iran was "ready to do whatever it deems necessary in response to their (the US's and Israel's) repeated aggression".So, how did an anonymous Indian account become the cited source for the Israeli information ecosystem? This was, incidentally, not the first time material had travelled between @RealBababanaras and Mossad Commentary. In at least two posts this year after Iran war began - one reporting continuing explosions in Iran after a US strike as evidence that missiles were stored there, and another which reported a US strike on an alleged uranium-enrichment and nuclear research facility - it cited @RealBababanaras as the source.As early as April, a month and a half after the US and Israel began air strikes in Iran, @RealBababanaras posted Tehran was preparing for its "first official nuclear test within weeks". Days later, @FalconUpdatesHQ, which has over 150,000 followers and claims in its bio to be based in Kerala, echoed that, claiming Iran was preparing to conduct its first official nuclear test within a month. The claim was recycled by @Im_Ritikaa in May.Earlier this year, Yonatan Hassidim, CEO of an Israeli firm that monitors and analyses online and social activity, said in an Israeli parliamentary hearing that about 70% of accounts sharing Netanyahu's posts in their sample were not Israelis at all. "That is to say, an Indian account shares a video of the Israeli prime minister speaking in Hebrew. Within 12 seconds, it has already understood that this item interests it - it apparently understands Hebrew - and shares it," he had said, before citing the example of an Indian account that "tweets more than 165,000 tweets a year"."So these are high volumes, and this is some kind of average account," he added, "We have seen ones with 300,000 a year and more as well."The loop is still active. On Aug 17, when US president Donald Trump posted on Truth Social the "no. 1 goal is, and always will be, that Iran cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon", @RealBababanaras repackaged this for its audience as a reaction "after Iran refused handing over enriched uranium and halting nuclear programme".
Article Summary: Hawkish narrative got significant boost from a fake quote. Fake quote first posted by an indian x handle, which then raced through tel aviv-washington political and diplomatic circles, right up to pm benjamin netanyahu and white house.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised India’s election system and called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, which seeks to require proof of citizenship and voter identification in US elections.In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a recent conversation involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and highlighted India’s use of photo identification for voters.Trump said, "Earlier this month, India’s Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration, How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?"Referring to the last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than 1 per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document."Trump also renewed his call for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, saying, "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!"According to the White House, the proposed legislation seeks to ensure that only US citizens are eligible to vote in federal elections. "American citizens and only American citizens should decide American elections," the White House said, describing the bill as a "common sense, bipartisan bill."The legislation would require voters to provide valid identification and proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. It also proposes limiting mail-in voting to certain circumstances, including illness, disability, military service and travel, according to news agency ANI.The White House said the bill would further require states to remove non-citizens from federal voter rolls. "If you want to register to vote in the United States, you have to be a citizen in the United States," it said.The administration also compared US election practices with those of other countries, arguing that the US has weaker voter-identification safeguards. "India and Brazil tie voter ID to a biometric database, while the United States largely relies on self-attestation for citizenship," the White House said.The bill was introduced in Congress on January 29. Trump has repeatedly backed the SAVE America Act, arguing that stricter voter-ID and citizenship requirements are necessary to strengthen election security.The SAVE America Act is a proposed US law aimed at tightening voting rules in federal elections. It would:MAGA supremo Donald Trump has urged both Republicans and Democrats to support the bill, arguing that only US citizens should decide US elections.The bill also compares US election rules with those in other countries. It says India and Brazil link voter IDs to biometric databases, while the US largely relies on self-attestation of citizenship. It also points to stricter ballot and mail-voting rules in countries such as Germany, Canada, Denmark and Sweden.

Article Title: In boost to Taliban ties, India joins in with victory day celebrations
Article Text:

NEW DELHI:In another expression of solidarity with Afghanistan, India participated in the fifth anniversary of the Taliban Victory Day that marks the return of the armed group to Kabul in August 2021, following the withdrawal of US-led forces.MEA joint secretary Anand Prakash - who handles the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) - represented India at the event held in the Afghan embassy. Prakash was accompanied by director (PAI) Sneha Dubey.India continues to maintain senior official-level engagement with the Taliban and as it looks to further ramp up its development presence there, a high-level visit to Kabul from India a little further down the line is also not ruled out. Standing next to the flag of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, the name used by Taliban for the country, charge d’affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor addressed a select gathering of diplomats, including ambassadors of neighbouring countries like Iran and Uzbekistan, and other dignitaries. Russian and Chinese diplomats also attended the event.Noor said in his remarks that stronger political trust, economic partnership, and continued engagement between Afghanistan and India will not only benefit both countries, but will also make an important contribution to regional stability, connectivity, and shared prosperity.The top Taliban diplomat here also thanked the MEA and minister S Jaishankar for their help in protecting and respecting the international rights of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, while seeking greater support from India.“We also appreciate their emphasis at international forums on the need to ensure Afghanistan’s legitimate international rights. We hope that greater attention and practical efforts will be made in this regard,” he said.India’s position on recognition of the regime in Kabul remains in consonance with that of the international community but the government allowed Taliban diplomats to take control of the embassy last year, while upgrading its own mission in Kabul. In the absence of official recognition, the main embassy flagpole still flies the flag of the previous Islamic Republic of Afghanistan but the Taliban are allowed to hold events in the embassy, like the press conference by foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi last year, under their own flag.Highlighting high-level visits from Afghanistan to India in the recent past, Noor also said that in recent years, relations between Afghanistan and India have witnessed significant progress, guided by “mutual respect, political engagement, and shared interests”.“Official diplomatic contacts between the two countries have expanded, embassies and consulates have become more active, and high-level delegations have continued to exchange visits. At the same time, constructive understanding has developed in the areas of political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation,” he said, adding that the 2 countries had reached understandings in various areas to expand bilateral cooperation.According to Noor, Afghanistan’s geography should not be a field for negative competition, but rather a bridge for connectivity, cooperation and shared prosperity. “Therefore, Afghanistan has continued its practical efforts to expand regional economic and transit cooperation, facilitate trade, and strengthen relations based on mutual interests,” he said.
Article Summary: India participated in the fifth anniversary of the taliban victory day that marks the return of the armed group to kabul in august 2021. India continues to maintain senior official-level engagement with the taliban. A high-level visit to kabul from india a little further down the line is also not ruled out.

Article Title: Chidambaram says he is 'proud to be a dimaagi Naxal'; BJP hits back
Article Text:
Sudhanshu Trivedi, P Chidambaram

Chidambaram's response to PM Modi

BJP-Congress clash over Naxalism

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi on Monday hit back at Congress leader P Chidambaram over his ‘dimagi Naxal’ remark, questioning the Congress' position on Naxalism by invoking former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's 2006 assessment of the threat.Trivedi said PM Modi had raised the issue in his Independence Day address and questioned Chidambaram's decision to embrace the label a day later."PM Modi raised a very important topic of 'Dimagi Naxal' on Independence Day. We are surprised that within 24 hours of this, Congress leader P Chidambaram has said that he is proud of being a 'Dimagi Naxal,'" Trivedi said.His remarks came a day after Chidambaram responded to PM Modi's Independence Day speech by saying, "I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!"Trivedi then cited a statement made by Manmohan Singh on April 13, 2006, when the former prime minister described Naxalism as a major internal security challenge.Also read - ‘Proud to be a dimagi naxal’: P Chidambaram hits back at PM Modi "I want to remind Congress and P Chidambaram that on 13th April 2006, former PM Dr Manmohan Singh said, "It would not be an exaggeration to say that the problem of Naxalism is the single biggest internal security challenge ever faced by our country"," Trivedi said."I want to ask the Congress - who was right, Dr Manmohan Singh or P Chidambaram?" he added.Chidambaram's remarks came after PM Modi, in his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, warned about what he described as a ‘dimagi naxal’ or Naxal mindset.PM Modi said armed Naxalism was nearing its end but cautioned that people with an ideological Naxal mindset could continue to pose a threat."Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path," PM Modi said.He also urged people to "identify and isolate" those he accused of seeking opportunities to promote violence and unrest.Chidambaram's response followed criticism from other Congress leaders over the Prime Minister's remarks. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused PM Modi of reviving labels such as "urban naxal" and "dimagi naxal" to target political opponents."First, you make derogatory remarks--calling them 'Urban Naxals' or 'Mental Naxals'--but later, you accept the very demands your political opponents were making," Ramesh said, according to ANI.The BJP has defended PM Modi's remarks and sought to frame the debate around internal security and ideological challenges, while the Congress has questioned the use of terms such as ‘dimagi Naxal’ against political critics.Trivedi's attack specifically sought to contrast the Congress' current response with the position taken by the Congress-led UPA government under Manmohan Singh.PM Modi had also said that the government had prioritised eliminating Naxalism since coming to power in 2014, claiming that decades of Maoist violence had damaged the lives and aspirations of young people and resulted in the deaths of security personnel."In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing," PM Modi said.The remarks have triggered a wider political debate over the distinction between armed Naxalism, ideological opposition and dissent, with opposition parties accusing the government of using the terminology to target its critics.The BJP has maintained that the term refers to individuals or ideological networks that it believes indirectly support or promote anti-national narratives.

Pm modi: "naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing" opposition parties accuse the government of using the terminology to target its critics.

Article Title: “We couldn’t be prouder”: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $5 million act of kindness turned their Texas roots into a lasting legacy
Article Text:
(Image via Brittany Mahomes/Instagram)

Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes turned their Texas connection into a lasting gift with their heartwarming effort

Patrick Mahomes continued supporting Texas Tech after becoming an NFL star

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes has built a remarkable football legacy, but some of his most meaningful moments have come away from the field. On Aug. 22, 2024, the Kansas City Chiefs star and his wife, Brittany Mahomes , made a $5 million contribution to Texas Tech’s South End Zone and Dustin R. Womble Football Center project. The gift helped push fundraising to $115 million and gave Mahomes another lasting connection to the university where his college football story began.Texas Tech announced the $5 million contribution on Aug. 22, 2024, as the final gift for its Campaign for Fearless Champions. The campaign began in 2014, when Patrick Mahomes was only a freshman at the university.The $242 million project includes the South End Zone and Dustin R. Womble Football Center. Texas Tech originally set a $100 million fundraising goal for the project, but Mahomes’ contribution pushed the total to $115 million.The university also gave Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes a permanent place inside the new facilities. The walkthrough area in the Dustin R. Womble Football Center will carry his name. His name will also appear on the quarterback meeting room and the offensive coordinator’s office in the new South End Zone Building connected to Jones AT&T Stadium.Kirby Hocutt, Texas Tech’s director of athletics, spoke about the contribution in the university’s announcement.“When we first launched this campaign, Patrick was only a freshman and now it is fitting that we approach the end of the campaign with a gift of his own,” Hocutt said. “We couldn't be prouder to announce this gift from Patrick and Brittany Mahomes.”The donation also connected with a much more personal part of Mahomes story. Patrick Mahomes was born in Tyler, Texas, and grew up in Whitehouse. Brittany Mahomes also attended Whitehouse High School, where the two met and began dating in 2012.Patrick Mahomes later took his football career to Texas Tech, playing for the Red Raiders from 2014 through 2016. That made the university an important part of his rise before Kansas City selected him 10th overall in the 2017 NFL Draft.Patrick Mahomes did not leave his connection to the Red Raiders behind when his NFL career took off. He returned to Texas Tech in 2022 for his induction into the school’s Hall of Fame and Ring of Honor during the Baylor game.He also continued making appearances at Red Raiders events when his Kansas City Chiefs schedule allowed. Texas Tech noted that Mahomes attended road games at Houston in 2021 and Kansas in 2023. He has also supported the school’s basketball and baseball programs during the NFL offseason.Joey McGuire, Texas Tech’s head football coach, spoke about Mahomes’ support in the university’s August 22, 2024 announcement.“There isn't a greater ambassador for Texas Tech Athletics than Patrick Mahomes,” McGuire said. He praised Mahomes for his success on the field and for what he and his family have done away from football.By August 2024, Mahomes had already won three Super Bowls with the Chiefs. He also earned Super Bowl MVP honors in each of those victories. Yet his connection to Texas Tech remained strong.The $5 million gift now gives that connection a permanent place on campus. The facilities will carry Mahomes’ name while supporting future Red Raiders, giving the university something that will remain long after his playing career ends.For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, the contribution was a way to support a school that played a major role in Patrick’s development. Their Texas roots began in Whitehouse, his college story continued in Lubbock, and the $5 million gift brought those two parts of his life together in a lasting way.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes and his wife, brittany mahomes, made a $5 million contribution to texas tech’s south end zone and dustin r. womble football center project. The gift helped push fundraising to $115 million and gave mahomes another lasting connection to the university where his college football story began.

Article Title: Trump's foreign policy: Strongmen on speed dial, allies and partners on notice
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from Washington

: Forget bombing Iran to end it as a civilization, US President Donald Trump on Sunday dropped bombshells on America's allies and partners, including India, to send a disquieting message: good ties with Washington may no longer guarantee its support in return.Within hours of each other, Trump warmly endorsed a new defence pact linking Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey while ordering a substantial reduction in US-South Korean military exercises, explicitly invoking his “very good relationship” with North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un. Taken together, the moves suggest a foreign policy increasingly organized around personal relationships, immediate transactional demands, and affinity for strongmen rather than the institutional logic of long-standing alliances.“Very happy to see” Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, Trump wrote on Truth Social, praising it as a step toward countries defending themselves “in a more meaningful way.” The pact commits the three to regard an armed attack on one as an attack on all and envisages deeper military cooperation.For India, the optics are particularly uncomfortable despite the much ballyhooed personal rapport between Trump and Modi.Pakistan’s military chief Asim Munir has cultivated an unusually close relationship with Trump and his family on the strength of a crypto outreach; Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan have likewise established strong personal channels with the president. Trump’s enthusiastic embrace of a pact involving Pakistan therefore contrasts sharply with Washington’s traditional effort to deepen India’s role as a democratic counterweight to China.The Mecca pact is not explicitly directed against India, and New Delhi has responded cautiously, saying it is studying its implications for national security and regional stability. Nor does Trump's endorsement amount to abandoning India. But the symbolism is unmistakable: Washington is applauding a new security architecture that is concerning to India even as he has virtually turned his back on Quad and unloaded against BRICS.The South Korea decision is even more startling. On Sunday, Trump said he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, which began Monday and involve about 18,000 South Korean troops. Trump complained about their cost, Seoul’s refusal to participate in US military action against Iran and, most revealingly, their supposed hostility toward a North Korea that he described as “unthreatening and respectful” because of his “very good relationship” with Kim.The irony is difficult to miss. South Korea is a treaty ally; North Korea is widely seen as a kooky nuclear-armed dictatorship that has supplied Russia with weapons and troops for its war in Ukraine. The exercises are designed precisely to maintain readiness against Pyongyang and now include training for drones, cyberwarfare, electronic warfare and GPS disruption.Richard Fontaine, president of the Center for a New American Security, called the administration's Asia policy increasingly incoherent, warning that excessive inconsistency could encourage countries to accommodate potential adversaries rather than rely on America. Victor Cha and Andy Lim of CSIS had earlier identified the underlying problem: Trump evaluates allies through transactional metrics -- defense spending and trade balances -- creating pressure for greater payments while threatening diminished security commitments.The pattern extends well beyond Asia. Neighbors Canada and Mexico has been subjected to extraordinary pressure from Trump, while European allies have faced tariffs, troop withdrawals and repeated questions about the value of NATO. Several foreign-policy analysts have expressed alarm at the developments, describing them as an increasingly transactional and damaging approach to America's traditional alliance system.Trump's defenders argue that this is not abandonment but burden-sharing: uncertainty is supposed to force allies to spend more on their own defense. MAGA activist Laura Loomer, a fringe element who is now an influential voice in Washington, offered precisely that kind of justification, arguing that South Korea should have helped Trump with Iran and that America's alliances depend on the unique personal authority Trump commands abroad.Yet that defense inadvertently makes the central problem clearer: if alliances and partnerships depend on personal ties with one president, they cease to be that in the traditional sense. The danger is not merely that Washington may lose friends; it is that friends may conclude they need insurance against Washington itself.Foreign policy mavens say that is the paradox of Trump's “America First” diplomacy : by making American protection conditional and personal, he may encourage allies from Seoul to New Delhi to Ottawa to Brussels to become more self-reliant and less dependent on America. Once allies and partners learn that lesson, they warn, rebuilding trust may prove considerably harder than destroying it.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump on sunday dropped bombshells on america's allies and partners, including india. Trump warmly endorsed a new defence pact linking saudi arabia, pakistan and turkey while ordering a substantial reduction in us-south korean military exercises.

Article Title: From Charles Haley to Von Miller: “Flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models” - Jerry Jones-led Dallas Cowboys’ history of taking chances on controversial stars
Article Text:
From Charles Haley to Von Miller: “Flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models” - Jerry Jones-led Dallas Cowboys’ history of taking chances on controversial stars(Image via X: Charles Haley and Von Miller​)

Jerry Jones-led Cowboys’ attraction to signing troubled past or controversial players like Charles Haley in 1992 and Von Miller in 2026

Von Miller’s controversial past includes a domestic violence case

Jerry Jones said in Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys that the physical and mental aspects of football are very complicated.“You’ve even heard it said, ‘You can’t play football successfully with Sunday school teachers.’ So, if you wait around and try to get the player with the perfect character, you’ve given yourself a handicap that’s not necessary. In fact, flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models,” Jones said.Charles Haley was known to scare coaches, while Von Miller has a troubled past, including a domestic violence case involving his then-girlfriend in 2023. Let’s check out these flawed individuals who were/can be rehabilitated, according to Jerry Jones.Charles Haley was a Pro Bowl player who had won two Super Bowls. The only problem he had was the horror stories coaches had heard about him.The legendary defensive end came with a troubled past of scolding coaches, being aggressive, and, plain and simple, being the torchbearer of horror stories.Haley himself admitted on Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys that he has three personalities within himself – Chuck [the a*sh*le], Charlie [the sensitive one who cries all the time], and Charles [the sensible one].“Let me give you a secret: whatever came into my head, I did. I didn’t give a sh*t,” he said.“Charles always found a rookie to pick on,” Bill Romanowski said on Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys. “When I got to the 49ers, I happened to be that rookie. You know, calling me a ‘p*ssy.’Then in 1992, I heard that Charles walked up into the general manager’s office; he pulled out his d*ck, pissed on his desk, and said, ‘This is how bad I want out of here.’”Jerry Jones admitted that it was “dicey” bringing Charles Haley from the San Francisco 49ers, but Jones is a huge believer in rehabilitation. So, he took the risk. And they won a Super Bowl that year! Not just one, but three! With Haley playing for them.Could this happen with Von Miller? He also comes with a troubled past. He also has two Super Bowls. He also happens to be an edge rusher! Can we stop here? Maybe not…Court documents obtained by WFAA in November 2023 reported that Von Miller was accused of assaulting his then-pregnant girlfriend at their high-rise apartment in Dallas.When police officers arrived at the scene, they found “minor abrasions” on Miller’s longtime girlfriend’s hand and bruising on her neck – “injuries consistent with applied pressure to the neck.”According to the arrest warrant affidavit, Miller and his girlfriend were arguing in their bedroom because she did not want to travel on her birthday that week. When the alleged victim went from the bedroom to the office, she slammed the office door in rage. This made Miller visibly angry.He went into the office and yelled at his girlfriend to “get out” of the apartment. The girlfriend began to comply with Miller’s request and attempted to gather her belongings when Miller began to shove and push her, all while telling her to leave the apartment.He then began to film her on his phone while continuing to push and shove her out of the home. She kept yelling, “Stop! I’m pregnant.” But Miller kept pushing. Then Miller applied pressure around the girlfriend’s neck for three to five seconds before letting go.The 911 call had her saying, “My boyfriend is choking and hitting me… I have bruises all over me, my hair is out.”When the dispatcher asked her about the boyfriend, she said, “He just stormed out.” The dispatcher then asked her if she needed paramedics; she said, “I don’t know. He pulled my hair out. I have, like, some blood on me… but not like…Yeah, I don’t know.”A warrant for a third-degree felony charge of assaulting a pregnant person was issued for Miller in November 2023, when he played for the Buffalo Bills.Miller turned himself in and was taken to the DeSoto Police Department jail for processing. He immediately posted a $5,000 bond and was released.Fast forward to today: the Dallas Cowboys have signed him for the 2026 season. Jerry Jones’ belief in rehabilitation is so strong; can this hypothetical modern-day Charles Haley lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl win? Especially after a 30-year drought? Remains to be seen…
Article Summary: Jerry jones-led cowboys’ attraction to signing troubled past or controversial players like charles haley in 1992 and von miller in 2026. Charles haley was known to scare coaches, while von miller has a troubled past, including a domestic violence case involving his then-girlfriend in 2023.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:
All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.​

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister mir ziaullah langove escaped unharmed. Six people, including three police personnel, were injured in the attack. The attack took place in the khad kocha area as langove was travelling from quetta to kalat.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the volhynia massacres. Campaign largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.
